Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

// https://www.lintcode.com/problem/binary-search-tree-iterator/description?_from=ladder&&fromId=1
/**
 * Definition of TreeNode:
 * class TreeNode {
 * public:
 *     int val;
 *     TreeNode *left, *right;
 *     TreeNode(int val) {
 *         this->val = val;
 *         this->left = this->right = NULL;
 *     }
 * }
 * Example of iterate a tree:
 * BSTIterator iterator = BSTIterator(root);
 * while (iterator.hasNext()) {
 *    TreeNode * node = iterator.next();
 *    do something for node
 */


class BSTIterator {
public:
    /*
    * @param root: The root of binary tree.
    */BSTIterator(TreeNode * root) {
        // do intialization if necessary
        TreeNode *cur = root;
        while(cur)
        {
            stack.push(cur);
            cur = cur->left;
        }
    }

    /*
     * @return: True if there has next node, or false
     */
    bool hasNext() {
        // write your code here
        return !stack.empty();
    }

    /*
     * @return: return next node
     */
    TreeNode * next() {
        // write your code here
        
        TreeNode *node = stack.top();
        stack.pop();
        
        TreeNode *cur = node->right;
        while(cur){
            stack.push(cur);
            cur = cur->left;
        }
        return node;
    }
    
private:
    std::stack<TreeNode *> stack;
    
};
